name: Price-Tag-Detection-And-Text-Grounding
description: A visual detection dataset of 200 images annotated with price-tag bounding boxes. It evaluates a model's ability to locate price tags in retail scenes, optionally guided by a text prompt.
card_text: Price-Tag-Detection-And-Text-Grounding is an image-text dataset for detecting price tags in retail imagery. Each sample includes a photograph of products or shelves, a generic user-style prompt, and an output list of bounding boxes labeled 'pricetag'. The bounding boxes are four-number coordinates that specify the location of each price tag. The images vary in scene complexity, lighting, and tag size, making the task one of open-set object detection/localization. The prompt field is a placeholder instruction that can be replaced by user-defined prompts for text grounding. The dataset is small (200 samples) and suitable for evaluating detection, localization, and visual grounding models. Outputs are structured as JSON-like objects rather than plain text, so systems must predict precise spatial coordinates for each price tag instance.

context.semantics: The main input image that the model must analyze. It shows a retail scene with one or more price tags to be detected and localized.

question.semantics: A generic prompt string ('users' specifically-defined prompts for different models') that serves as the textual instruction accompanying the image. It can be replaced by user-defined prompts for grounding tasks.

image.semantics: File path to the input image containing retail products and price tags. It is the visual input for detection.

bbox.semantics: Bounding-box annotations for price tags. Each item is a dictionary with the key 'pricetag' mapped to a four-number coordinate list [x, y, w, h] (or [x1, y1, x2, y2]) locating a single price tag in the input image.

meta.meta_structure_description: Each sample consists of an input object with an image_file path and a generic prompt, plus an output object containing a bbox list. The image_file provides the visual context; the prompt is a short instruction. The bbox list contains one or more dictionaries, each mapping the label 'pricetag' to a four-number coordinate list that defines a price-tag bounding box. The model must predict these boxes from the image and prompt.
